questions.question: Explain what an orbit is and how long the Earth takes to complete one.
questions.expected_answer: An orbit is the path a planet follows as it travels around the Sun. The Earth takes one year, about three hundred and sixty-five days, to complete one orbit.

questions.question: Why is the Sun at the centre of the solar system, and what keeps the planets in their orbits?
questions.expected_answer: The Sun is the biggest object in the solar system, and all the planets travel around it. Its strong pull, called gravity, pulls the planets towards it, and because the planets are also moving fast, they keep going around the Sun instead of falling into it or flying away.

questions.question: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun.
questions.expected_answer: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
